origins.section: 7.4 Keys Live Under the Module's Master Key and Are Known by Their Check Value
7.4.1 Two Modules, One Key, Different Bytes
7.2 A PIN Block Means Nothing Without Its Key and Its Card Number
7.5 A MAC Covers the Bytes as Sent, So It Is the Last Thing You Add
7.7 Card Data Crosses the Client Intact and Stays Nowhere

gates.says: all 5 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-missing-provider: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-missing-provider: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-missing-provider: Section 7.4 says that on Java 17, without the provider line, the module is 'not registered', Q2 logs the SunJCE warning once and 'carries on deploying everything else', and the first lookup throws NameRegistrar.NotFoundException, which is option c.
recorded.prompt:q-key-bytes: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-key-bytes: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-key-bytes: Section 7.4.1 shows the same key with different bytes in the two modules but the same check value EB7A8D, and says 'compare that, never the bytes', which is option a.
recorded.prompt:q-tls-instead: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-tls-instead: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-tls-instead: Section 7.2 says TLS decrypts the bytes 'into the process that receives them, which logs them, queues them and passes them on', and section 7.3 says decrypting the PIN in the application puts clear PINs in the heap, which together decide option a.
recorded.prompt:q-field7-after-mac: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-field7-after-mac: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-field7-after-mac: Section 7.5 says to sign last because 'any change after signing, however harmless it looks, makes the host reject the message', and section 7.8 says 'One change after signing and the host answers 63', which is option a.
recorded.prompt:q-masked-pan: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-masked-pan: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-masked-pan: Section 7.7 shows field 2 as 411111______1111 packed by jPOS 'without complaint' and says 'The host receives a card number it can't authorize, and declines', which is option a.

recorded.prompt:q-missing-provider:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-missing-provider:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-missing-provider:a: Section 7.4 says the provider line 'is required' on Java 17 because the default SunJCE load by class name is something 'the JDK no longer lets outside code do', so the module does not start and nothing works as it did on Java 8.
recorded.prompt:q-missing-provider:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-missing-provider:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-missing-provider:b: Section 7.4 ties 'every MAC fails' only to the case where the package is opened with --add-exports; without that the module is 'not registered (hsm-no-provider)'.
recorded.prompt:q-missing-provider:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-missing-provider:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-missing-provider:d: Section 7.4 says the warning is logged 'once, as a warning while Q2 starts' and the failure shows at the first lookup; that this rules out retries is a short inference, since the page never mentions retries explicitly.
recorded.prompt:q-key-bytes:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-key-bytes:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-key-bytes:b: Section 7.4.1 says the reverse: the bytes differ because they are under different LMKs, and the check values match.
recorded.prompt:q-key-bytes:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-key-bytes:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-key-bytes:c: Section 7.4.2 shows a mistyped ZMK importing the same transport bytes as a different key (check value 8D6B46 instead of 6D0613 once the parity check is off), so identical transport digits prove nothing about the key; reading the example this way takes a short inference.
recorded.prompt:q-key-bytes:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-key-bytes:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-key-bytes:d: Section 7.4.2 says directly: 'Matching ZMK check values only say the ceremony went right. They say nothing about the key that arrives next... so compare each new key's own check value too.'
recorded.prompt:q-tls-instead:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-tls-instead:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-tls-instead:b: Section 7.2 says TLS 'encrypts a connection' and places the exposure at each end after decryption, not in the records; refuting the option's claim about the records takes a short inference.
recorded.prompt:q-tls-instead:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-tls-instead:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-tls-instead:c: Section 7.3 says the card schemes 'allow a clear PIN only inside a secure device', so a clear PIN in an ordinary client process fails a PIN audit whether or not the process is trusted.
recorded.prompt:q-tls-instead:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-tls-instead:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-tls-instead:d: Section 7.2 says that at each end the bytes are decrypted into the receiving process, so the PIN would not be plain only inside encrypted records.
recorded.prompt:q-field7-after-mac:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-field7-after-mac:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-field7-after-mac:b: Section 7.5 defines the MAC as computed 'with a key both sides share, the ZAK', so field 7 is not part of the key.
recorded.prompt:q-field7-after-mac:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-field7-after-mac:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-field7-after-mac:c: This is only inference: the page never discusses replay checks, but section 7.5 attributes a 63 after a post-signing change to the MAC, and the stem's field 7 holds the current time, not an old one.
recorded.prompt:q-field7-after-mac:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-field7-after-mac:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-field7-after-mac:d: This is inference: section 7.5 says the MAC covers the packed message as the host's spec defines it, with no mention of the PIN key, and the stem says purchases without a PIN also get 63.
recorded.prompt:q-masked-pan:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-masked-pan:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-masked-pan:b: Section 7.7 says the host 'declines' the masked card number, which contradicts an approval.
recorded.prompt:q-masked-pan:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-masked-pan:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-masked-pan:c: Section 7.7 says 'jPOS packs the result without complaint' and shows the packed message.
recorded.prompt:q-masked-pan:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-masked-pan:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-masked-pan:d: This is a short inference: the page never mentions the MUX, but section 7.7 says 'The host receives a card number', so the message was sent.
